title: QuickFixSmith: sandboxed shortflow composer and runbook-as-task adapter
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Build QuickFixSmith: an interactive sandbox and composer that converts incident playbooks into safe, replayable 'shortflows' (taskified runbooks). The system will let oncall and first-line support create, test, and publish shortflows which execute against a staged environment or a dry-run harness. The adapter will expose a runbook-as-task API that hooks into the existing ops task runner and provides declarative parameter validation, RBAC gating, telemetry hooks, and automatic rollback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Users can author a shortflow in the sandbox UI and persist it as a versioned artifact with metadata and owner
Shortflows can be executed in dry-run mode that validates side-effecting steps without changing production state
Runbook-as-task API exposes a stable POST endpoint and SDK wrapper; tasks appear in the ops task queue and have observable execution traces
RBAC and audit logging are enforced: only allowed roles can publish or run shortflows; all executions append audit entries to the central log
Telemetry captures per-step latency, error classification, and tokenized command traces for later replay investigations
steps: Spec: outline JSON schema for shortflow DSL, inputs, outputs and safe-ops markers (owner: Sara)
Sandbox: implement isolated nodejs service + ephemeral stub environment for dry-run execution (owner: Backend team)
Adapter: build /v1/ops/shortflows endpoint, map to existing task runner contract with idempotency and retries (owner: Infra)
RBAC/Audit: integrate with SSO groups and central audit pipeline; add KMS tagging for sensitive steps (owner: Security)
UI: composer with step templates, parameter validation, and playback simulator (owner: UX)
E2E tests: create fixture harness using incident snapshot dataset and run synthetic regressions against telemetry outputs
recent_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting — agreed on two-mode execution (dry-run vs live) and strict safety markers for any step that mutates state.
2025-02-14: Draft DSL schema submitted to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/quickfixsmith/dsl-v1 — feedback requested from Security and Platform.
2025-02-18: Prototype sandbox backend up (stub runner + fake resources). Demoed to oncall team; they requested richer parameter typing and replay snapshots.
2025-02-21: PR #1284 opened for adapter skeleton: github.com/redwood/ops/pull/1284 — awaiting code review from @alicia and @mike.

2025-02-24: Security review notes: require explicit KMS label on any step referencing credentials; block publish without review for high-risk tags. Adding gating ticket to implement KMS label enforcement.
notes: Trade-offs: prefer a conservative DSL surface now and iterate; avoid including arbitrary shell execution — use an allowed-ops whitelist mapped to internal SDK calls.
Safety: every mutating step must declare a rollback action; the publish flow requires either a peer-review or an automated static analysis pass.
Testing plan: create a set of 12 canonical incident snapshots derived from past incidents; run nightly dry-run regression and report delta signals to the regression alert channel.
Fallback: when a shortflow execution fails, the adapter must trigger the existing incident escalation policy and capture an execution dump for replay.
